title: Uniform affine truncation for all quasi-coherent derived objects
statement: Let f:X→Y be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] and higher direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For every integer q and affine open U of Y there exists an integer a such that, for every E in D_QCoh(O_X), restricting H^q(Rf_*) of the canonical projection E→tau_≥a E to U is an isomorphism of sheaves of modules on U. The integer a depends only on f,q,U, not on E.

source.place: Tag 08DZ, local uniform truncation argument, using Tag 08D5(2)

proof.text: Set V=f^{-1}(U) and g=f|U. Choose the standard derived categories on V and U. They have the same sheaf-of-modules carriers as the existing constructions. The morphism g remains qcqs and its affine target is compact. Form the exact restriction functors F and G by overFunctor followed by Scheme.Modules.overEquiv. Their homology comparison and overFunctorEquiv identify the homology of F(E) with restriction of the homology of E. Quasi-coherence is preserved by the proved Mathlib isQuasicoherent_restrictFunctor instance.

Apply the first clause of the uniform truncation bound to g, obtaining N. Put n=N-q. For each restricted object K, let T=tau_<(-n)K. Zero module sheaves are quasi-coherent (the free sheaf on the empty type), so homologyProperty_truncLE and truncLEIsoTruncLT give quasi-coherent cohomology of T. Shift stability gives the same for T[-n-1]. The t-structure shift bound puts this shifted object in degrees at most zero. Apply N in degree j+n+1, then use derived direct-image shift compatibility and homology shiftIso to conclude H^j(Rg_*T)=0 for j=q and q+1. The homology exact sequence of the mapped distinguished truncation triangle makes its middle map an isomorphism.

Use the natural open-restriction comparison Rf_* followed by derived G isomorphic to derived F followed by Rg_*. Compose it with mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso to obtain a comparison of higher-direct-image functors. Exact F commutes with truncGE via mapDerivedCategoryTruncGEIso; its inverse component factors F of the canonical projection, by pi_descTruncGE. Mapping this factorization gives an isomorphism under Rg_* cohomology. Naturality of the higher-direct-image comparison transports it to G of the original higher-direct-image map. Finally overEquiv reflects isomorphisms, giving the overFunctor map. This is uniform in E and includes zero objects and empty U.

theorem exists_isIso_schemeHigherDirectImage_uniform_truncGE_over_affine
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (q : ℤ) (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
      IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) U).map
        ((schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ a).app E.obj)))
